collection_notes: Steps 1-5 were run identically for every candidate in the US Senate, US House 1-6 and Governor races (the shared WebSearch budget ran out once mid-run and the remaining searches were completed after it reset). To keep effort equal, no T3 items are included for any candidate in these races: every item comes from the T1 voters' pamphlet, official .gov pages or official roll-call pages; promising T3 results are named in these notes for possible later, race-wide use. Campaign websites are recorded from the pamphlet but were not fetched for positions, for any candidate. oregonlive.com and apnews.com are rejected by the search proxy as allowed_domains, so step 5 used three fixed domain groups for everyone: (opb, oregoncapitalchronicle, wweek, ballotpedia), (kgw, koin, kptv, katu), (portlandmercury, vote411, pamplinmedia, portlandtribune). The Multnomah military/overseas online voters' guide was checked and contains no federal or governor statements. Pamphlet excerpts were obtained through a summarizing fetch limited to ~125-character quotes, so excerpts are short. Incumbency: pamphlet occupation 'U.S. Congresswoman' and 'U.S. Congress (2024-present)'. Ballot spelling 'Janelle S Bynum' matches inventory. Note: on the Laken Riley Act (v2) she voted Yea, unlike the other Oregon Democrats. KATU 'Your Voice Your Vote' (2026-10-10) features Bynum and Adair, and KOIN has general-election issue interviews with both; not fetched, to keep T3 treatment identical across all assigned races (Townsend is not in them).
